title: finding(components): three thin `page:*` containers keep the retired `body` arm — the question is the STORED corpus, which this repository cannot read
body:
Restart-when: a reading of the STORED corpus exists for `body` on `page:section` / `page:footer` / `page:sidebar` — taken by a seat or tool that can see tenant documents, with a control that FIRES (the `card`+`body` population is 40 and lives in Markdown fences and .tsx fixtures, not only .json), and `page:sidebar` counted separately from `ui:sidebar`

（由分诊席按 hold 定级写入;依据见评论 5734161571。）

Dedupe words: `page:section body` · `page:footer body` · `page:sidebar body` · stored-corpus reading · `PageContainerProps` children-only

Surfaced by the `os-dev` delivering objectui#6771 (PR objectui#9895) — which **drafted the removal, reverted it, and escalated rather than shipping a zero from an instrument whose control did not fire**. The readings below are the dev's, ⛔ not re-derived by this seat; what this seat verified is that the arms are restored on head `42a139a1` with the escalation written inline (`containers.tsx:1132-1140`, `:2247`, `:2274`). ⛔ Not graded, ⛔ not routed.

## The question, and why it cannot be answered from this repository

objectui#6771 retires the `body` child-list dialect. Every consumer dropped its `body` arm **except four**: `page:card` (grounded — see below) and three thin containers, `page:section` · `page:footer` · `page:sidebar` (`packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx:1140`, `:2247`, `:2274`).

**The authoring-face argument for dropping them is good**: the spec declares all three through one `PageContainerProps` whose single key is `children`; they were `EmptyProps` before that; this side registered them with **no `inputs` at all**. ⇒ `body` was never published for them on either face.

⚠️ **But that answers the wrong face.** What `page-container-authorable-keys.test.tsx` pins, and what `page:card`'s own surviving read is grounded on (objectstack#5775, the ADR-0087 D2 **load-time conversion**), is the **stored** corpus: documents already saved by tenants. Deleting a read before the conversion is live blanks an existing page's content **silently**.

## ⭐ The instrument that failed, recorded because it is the reusable lesson

The dev built a corpus scan to settle it. Against the pre-retirement tree it returned **zero** for the three — **and its control returned zero too**, for a population that is actually **40** (`card` + `body`), because the walk opened only `.json` while those 40 live in Markdown fences and `.tsx` fixtures. Two of its four `sidebar` hits were `ui:sidebar`, not `page:sidebar` — the bare-vs-namespaced confusion this family's history already records twice.

⇒ 「a zero from an instrument whose control is silent is not a reading」. The dev nearly shipped that zero's answer and did not.

## What was done instead, and the asymmetry that decided it

The arms are **kept**, with the escalation written where a reader meets it. The costs are not symmetric: deleting an arm that **does** have a stored population blanks content silently — the least reportable failure there is; keeping one that does **not** leaves a visible dialect in three thin containers, removable later at **no risk**.

## What this card wants

A reading of the **stored** corpus — do any saved documents author `body` on `page:section` / `page:footer` / `page:sidebar`? — taken by a seat or a tool that can see tenant documents, ⛔ not by grepping this repository.

- **Zero there** ⇒ the three arms can be deleted outright, and this card closes with that reading attached.
- **Non-zero** ⇒ they ride the same ADR-0087 D2 load-time conversion as `page:card`, and this card becomes a pointer on that conversion's work item.

⚠️ ⛔ Not measured here and named so it is not read as clean: whether any renderer BEYOND these four still reads the retired key. The at-tier contract review of PR objectui#9895 re-derived the population with a spelling-agnostic probe; this card takes its scope from that and ⛔ does not re-assert it.

⛔ Not deduped by this seat — the filer attaches the words and triage runs them.
